# Version Retrospective – v1.7.0 — Sample Prompts Library
This document reflects on what worked, what didn't, and how future versions can be improved.

## Version Summary

Shipped a curated sample-prompts library to remove the "what should I type?" friction for first-time and returning users. Eight seed prompts (4 triggers + 4 skips) live in `public/sample-prompts.json` — hand-editable, no rebuild needed. The UI is two surfaces: an inline pill row above the chat input (visible on empty state, collapsed after first send) and a "See all" modal with category filter chips and a 3-bar complexity meter on each card.

Seven features delivered (F45–F51): JSON + loader, inline pill row, collapsed-state pill, See-all modal, confirm-replace mini-modal (via the existing `showConfirm()` helper), complexity meter, and welcome slide 4 update. Defensive loading + content-safety pass + a11y pass all completed during Phase 6.

Execution mode departed from the original tasklist plan: USER chose to run all 7 phases end-to-end without per-phase smoke tests, doing one comprehensive test at the end. This worked well for this version — the surface area is largely additive (one new JSON file, one new section in styles.css, one new section in app.js, two new blocks in index.html, plus three small surgical edits to existing code) — but is worth being deliberate about for future versions that touch more existing code paths.

## What Went Well

- **Mockup-first workflow.** Locking the design via the interactive HTML mockup at `mockups/option-c-inline-with-see-all.html` before any production-code work was a real time-saver. Three iterations of design feedback (red→amber color, fixed modal height, `+` button sizing, JSON ordering, complexity meter) all happened on the mockup, not on the live app. Implementation was largely a port.
- **Reuse of existing confirm modal.** The `showConfirm({ title, body, okLabel, cancelLabel, okVariant })` Promise-returning helper from v1.6.0 (Caching Lock work) generalized cleanly to a third use case (Replace current message?). No refactor needed — the API was already option-based. Saved a parallel modal.
- **CSS variable conventions held.** Adding `--triggers` and `--skips` to the existing `:root` block and using `var()` references throughout kept the new section visually consistent with the rest of the app palette without ad-hoc color values scattered through the CSS.
- **Defensive loading caught a real edge case during design.** The "what if `sample-prompts.json` is missing" question surfaced during the design doc phase, not after deployment. The filter-then-warn pattern (each entry validated independently; bad entries skipped with a `console.warn`) means a single malformed prompt won't blow up the whole library.
- **textContent / createTextNode everywhere for prompt-derived strings.** This was a deliberate decision documented in the design doc's Security section, and it held all the way through implementation. The whole feature is XSS-safe by construction even if someone forks the repo and points it at user-generated JSON.
- **JSON ordering decision.** Reordering the seed prompts (3 triggers + 2 skips visible inline) over alternating or all-triggers-first is a small detail that matters a lot for first-launch discoverability — users immediately see both categories rather than scrolling past the See-all pill to find a skip example. Worth the 30 seconds of thought.
- **Color choice (amber over red for skips).** The user's initial instinct was red; pushing back with the "skips isn't a failure mode, just a category" framing and proposing the existing `--eval-accent` amber color produced a better-looking and more semantically correct result. Worth pushing back on color decisions when conventions would mislead.

## What Could Have Gone Better

- **Tooltip styling on pills relied on `position: relative` + `:hover .sp-tooltip` in CSS.** On narrow viewports the tooltip can clip off the left or right edge of the pill row container. Not a blocker, but the mockup uses `max-width: 360px` which can still overflow if a pill is near the right edge. A future polish item: anchor the tooltip with viewport-aware positioning or use the native `title` attribute as a fallback for the trickiest narrow cases.
- **Complexity meter placement: modal-only on pills, but added to the pill tooltip mid-test.** The Q5 resolution left "complexity in inline pills" as an implementer's call. The first decision was "leave it modal-only" because pills are visually compact. During USER testing, we revisited and added the 3-bar meter to the **pill hover tooltip** instead — same visual, only revealed on hover, so the pills stay clean while complexity is one hover away from the inline row. Lesson: when an open question has a "leave it for now" resolution, expect a follow-up nudge once the feature is in the user's hands and be ready to adjust.
- **Welcome-seen key bump (`v1` → `v2`) is a coarse signal.** Anyone who has dismissed the welcome before will see it again now. For most users this is fine (the new slide 4 wording really is the reason for showing it). But if welcome content changes every version, the key keeps bumping and existing users will see the welcome repeatedly. A future enhancement: track the *content* version (a hash of slide bodies) rather than a manual integer, so we only re-show when content actually changed.
- **No native dropdown for managing custom prompts.** Users can add their own prompts by editing the JSON file directly, which is fine for the playground's audience (developers). But a non-trivial fraction of users will probably want a UI for adding/editing. Out of scope for v1.7.0; flag for a possible v1.8.x if user feedback supports it.
- **Tasklist had per-phase USER smoke tests that we ended up consolidating.** The all-at-once execution mode the user chose worked here, but it meant Phase 1's "verify static serving" check, Phase 3's "tooltip works" check, etc. all collapsed into the final comprehensive test. If something broke mid-phase, we'd have caught it only at the end. For more complex versions, the original per-phase pattern is probably safer.

## Mid-test scope additions (folded into v1.7.0)

Six items landed during USER testing rather than as separate patches. All small, all cohesive with the version goals, but together they made v1.7.0 noticeably broader than the locked design doc anticipated:

1. **Complexity legend in the modal footer.** USER asked for an at-a-glance explanation of the 3-bar meter. Added a second row in `.sp-modal-footer` showing each tier's mini-meter + label + token range, always visible (no hover required).
2. **Complexity meter in the pill hover tooltip.** Pairs the tier visual with the triggers/skips badge inside the tooltip. Closes the loop on Q5 — complexity is now reachable from the inline row, just not on the pill chrome itself.
3. **Cursor `?` / native-title-tooltip fix.** Original code set `cursor: help` on `.sp-complexity-meter` to hint at a hover tooltip, but native `title`-based tooltips have a ~1s delay and felt broken. Removed `cursor: help`, baked the token-range explanations into always-visible text (card hint line + footer legend + pill tooltip). No hidden affordance, no slow tooltips.
4. **GPT-5.5 evaluator bump + pricing correction.** Scope creep, but tiny: bumped `EVAL_MODEL_OPENAI` from `gpt-5.4` to `gpt-5.5` across 8 references (server constant, Settings hint, dropdown label, cost-estimates blurb, `PRICES` table, README × 3). Live-verified pricing on the OpenAI page and caught a wrong placeholder — gpt-5.5 is $5 in / $30 out per MTok, not $5/$15. Per-eval cost estimate bumped accordingly.
5. **OpenAI pricing URL added to `/check-advisor-tool-updates`.** Catch-up script now WebFetches the OpenAI pricing page as a 4th source, scoped strictly to the playground's evaluator model. Reference doc grew a new **OpenAI Evaluator Pricing** subsection mirroring the Anthropic Pricing Snapshot format. Future catch-up runs will surface evaluator pricing / flagship drift the same way they surface advisor-tool API drift.
6. **Sentinel-marker strip on the advisor branch + newline collapse on all strip paths.** USER noticed the Full I/O viewer still showed `<!-- advisor:only -->` tags on the advisor branch even though Code View had been stripping them. Added a `stripSentinelMarkers()` helper in `server.js` matching the Code View regex exactly, applied it to the advisor branch's outgoing `params.system`. Then USER asked about the `\n\n` runs (paragraph breaks in the Recommended preset content), so all three strip functions now collapse `\n+` to a single space + collapse double-spaces. The system prompt sent to the API is now one continuous line. Tiny token saving, but more importantly Code View and the real request now produce identical output.

**Net effect:** v1.7.0 ended up doing more than its design doc described, all in directions the USER asked for during testing. Worth being explicit about this for future versions — testing surfaces things; budget a little slack for mid-build refinements rather than treating the design doc as a hard contract.

## Lessons Learned

- **Honest pushback on user proposals saves time when the proposal would mislead.** Red for "skips advisor" felt natural to the user, but red-as-error is a deeply entrenched UI convention. Pushing back with "those aren't bad prompts" and proposing amber from the existing palette took ~2 messages and produced a better outcome than implementing red and then redoing it.
- **"This is a version, not a patch"** is worth saying out loud when the scope warrants it. The user explicitly asked which it should be — being decisive about the answer (and citing the comparison to v1.5.0's Code View modal in scope and surface area) prevented us from trying to cram this into a patch flow that's optimized for one-or-two-file changes.
- **The interactive mockup paid for itself many times over.** All eight UX questions (color, label, button size, modal height, search vs. filter, complexity meter design, JSON ordering, tooltip behavior) were resolved on the mockup before any production-code work began. Rebuilding this in production would have taken 5–10× as long.
- **The version-bump-checklist memory continues to be load-bearing.** This is the third version where the checklist has caught at least one place that would otherwise have been missed (this time: `package-lock.json`'s inner `packages[""].version` field). The v1.6.2 patch added `docs/build/feature-backlog.md` to the checklist after we caught it missing; this version benefited from that addition.
- **CSS class prefixing (`sp-` for sample-prompts) prevented a class-name collision.** Initially the mockup used generic class names like `.prompt-pill`, `.prompt-card`, etc. The implementation switched to `sp-*` prefixes to avoid colliding with any existing or future class. Small thing, but it eliminated a whole category of "why is this style being overridden" bugs.

## Action Items

- **Consider a settings-modal section for "Custom prompts".** If user feedback suggests demand, add a section in the Settings modal that lets users CRUD their own prompts (stored in localStorage, merged with the JSON file's defaults). Out of scope for v1.7.0; revisit after seeing real usage.
- **Smarter welcome-seen versioning.** Hash the slide content and use that as the seen-key suffix, so we only re-show when content actually changed. Track as a low-priority backlog item.
- **Complexity in inline pills (the pill chrome itself, not the tooltip).** Resolved during v1.7.0: complexity ships in the pill tooltip + the modal cards + the modal-footer legend, but not on the pill body itself. Revisit if the library grows past ~12 prompts and users want it on the pill body for at-a-glance scanability without hover.
- **Tooltip viewport-edge handling.** If we get reports of clipped tooltips on narrow viewports, switch to viewport-aware positioning or fall back to native `title` attribute. Low priority — current behavior is acceptable.
- **Document the JSON schema in the README more visibly.** The README has a one-line mention; consider expanding to a small "Adding your own prompts" subsection if user feedback shows people are trying.
